about: Every hosted cache key class this repository writes: who saves it, how large it may grow, and how it is allowed to churn. Read by scripts/lib/workflow_cache_budget_gate.py (the workflows must agree with it, both directions) and by scripts/lib/cache_prune.py (the pruner). A cache nobody declared here is an orphan and the pruner deletes it.
target_note: GitHub evicts least-recently-used entries once the repository passes cap_mb, and it does not know that the RocksDB engine (5 MB, about 290 s to rebuild) is worth more than a 600 MB target directory. The class budgets are therefore held at or below target_mb (85 percent of the cap) so that this repository, not LRU, decides what is dropped. Measured on 2026-10-09 the repository held 10.78 GB in 46 entries with six more already evicted; the budgets below sum to 8.3 GB after the readers and dropped entries are applied.

classes.note: One entry per (source pin, recipe, compiler). A miss rebuilds the engine in about 290 s and trips the job-budget margin of the ci job. Written only from the default branch and only on a miss; never deleted by the size pass; the previous generation is kept for one key bump.
West workspace plus SDK, keyed by the Zephyr ref, SDK version and python version. Restoring takes about 55 s against a multi-minute cold fetch; the key moves only when a pin moves.

The pinned zenohd and zenoh-c builds and the generated opaque-size tables. Each is a pure function of a version plus a script hash and each is a source build: the unixpipe and vsock routers took 292 s each to rebuild in three of the last four interop runs because the entry had been evicted (6 MB each).

Downloaded .debs per job. The key carries the workflow hash and the run id because a cache entry is immutable: a changed package list needs a new key. Saved only when apt actually downloaded something, so a warm run adds nothing. This is the one class allowed to carry github.run_id; the pruner keeps the newest entry of each job and drops the rest.

The one workspace dependency cache for the Linux feature-set jobs. The ci job saves it; the readers restore it and never save, so one manifest change writes one entry instead of eight. The old arrangement gave every job its own key because several parallel SAVERS thrash a shared key; a shared key with a single saver does not. Each reader's worst case is its own cold run, which the 18-run measurement puts at 13-26 minutes against budgets of 30-45.
The workspace plus the sce-codegen and xtask build set. Warm saves about 6 minutes of a 17 minute job.
The best payback of any private entry: about 9 of 23 minutes cold, against a 30 minute ceiling.
Its own environment (a different rust-cache environment hash), so nothing else can read it. Warm saves about 8 of 32 minutes: the best ratio of any entry.
A cold run takes 23 of its 30 minutes; the entry is small.

Workspace plus the oracles tree (R2625: without it the whole of zenoh rebuilds from source every run). Its own rust-cache environment hash, because the job installs a second toolchain, so the ci entry cannot stand in for it.
Registry only (the lanes build into per-lane target dirs). One key, saved by shard 0 and restored by all four shards; it used to be four identical entries.
The two Zephyr Rust workspaces, one entry each.

Windows and macOS dependency cache, one entry per host (the host is part of the rust-cache key). The Platform lane's leg saves it, with cache-on-failure because that lane is read while red; portability (ci.yml) and capi read it. The three jobs built one workspace and kept three copies.
Its own environment hash on both hosts (it installs the router toolchain), so the host-workspace entry cannot serve it.
